FAQ.a0: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol developed by Anthropic that allows AI models to securely connect to external data sources and tools. MCP standardizes the interaction between AI and various services.
FAQ.q1: How do I install an MCP server?
FAQ.a1: Installing an MCP server is typically done via npm or another package manager. Most servers have detailed documentation with installation and configuration instructions in the repository's README file.
FAQ.q2: How does MCP differ from traditional APIs?
FAQ.a2: Unlike traditional APIs, where a developer manually integrates endpoints, MCP provides a standardized way for AI models to automatically discover and use available tools and data.
FAQ.a3: MCP is supported in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, as well as various code editors and AI tools. The list of supported clients is constantly growing.
FAQ.q4: Can I create my own MCP server?
FAQ.a4: Yes, you can create your own MCP server using SDKs for TypeScript, Python, or other languages. The MCP SDK provides all the necessary tools for server development.
FAQ.a5: MCP is designed with security in mind. The user always controls which servers are running and what permissions they have. Each server runs in an isolated process.

AboutMcp.metaDescription: A detailed explanation of Model Context Protocol (MCP) — an open protocol for integrating AI assistants with external tools, databases, and services.
AboutMcp.metaKeywords: MCP, Model Context Protocol, AI protocol, MCP servers, what is MCP
AboutMcp.ogDescription: A detailed explanation of the MCP protocol for AI integrations
AboutMcp.intro: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol developed by Anthropic to standardize interaction between AI assistants and external data sources, tools, and services.
AboutMcp.whyMcpP1: Before MCP, each AI integrator created their own way to connect to external systems. This led to fragmentation: the same integrations had to be rebuilt for each AI client.
AboutMcp.whyMcpP2: MCP solves this problem by providing a unified standard. Now it's enough to write an MCP server once, and it will work with any MCP-compatible client: Claude Desktop, Cursor, Continue, Cline, and many others.
AboutMcp.archServer: MCP Server — provides tools, resources, and prompts
AboutMcp.archClient: MCP Client — an AI application that connects to servers
AboutMcp.archTransport: Transport — stdio, SSE (Server-Sent Events), or HTTP
AboutMcp.capabilitiesIntro: An MCP server can provide three types of capabilities:
AboutMcp.capTools: Tools — functions that AI can invoke to perform actions (search, write data, send messages)
AboutMcp.capResources: Resources — data that AI can read (files, databases, API responses)
AboutMcp.capPrompts: Prompts — ready-made request templates for typical tasks
AboutMcp.exampleDbDesc: AI can execute SQL queries, get table schemas, and analyze data without direct database access.
AboutMcp.exampleDocsDesc: AI gains access to internal company documentation and can answer questions based on current data.
AboutMcp.exampleInfraDesc: AI can read logs, restart services, and check metrics through integration with Kubernetes, AWS, Docker.
AboutMcp.exampleFilesDesc: AI can read, create, and edit files in the project through the MCP server's file system.
AboutMcp.securityIntro: MCP is designed with security in mind:
AboutMcp.secConfirm: Each tool requires explicit user confirmation
